title: Characterization of Herschel-selected strong lens candidates through HST and sub-mm/mm observations
question: Confirm the gravitational lensing nature of 281 Herschel-selected candidate strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxies using HST F110W snapshot observations and archival sub-mm/mm data, and characterize the lens properties and reconstructed near-IR background sources.

data.bands: Band 3, Band 4, Band 5, Band 6, Band 7, Band 8

(2018), when available, if not, we adopt the flux densities published in the H-ATLAS Data Release 1 (DR1, Valiante et al. 2016) or Data Release 2 (DR2, Maddox et al. 2018).

recipe.goal: Reduce HST WFC3/F110W snapshot observations and apply astrometric correction
recipe.method: Flatfield correction, background subtraction, cosmic-ray cleaning, distortion correction, rotation, drizzling with 4-point sub-pixel dithering, and matching Gaia eDR3 sources to HST counterparts.
key_parameters: output pixel size = 0.064 arcsec; FOV = 136 arcsec x 123 arcsec

recipe.goal: Classify lens candidates via visual inspection and multiwavelength archival data
recipe.method: Visual inspection of HST images, cross-matching with high-resolution ALMA, SMA, and NOEMA continuum images to identify multiple images/arcs or unlensed DSFGs, and updating classification after lens subtraction.

recipe.goal: Model and subtract foreground lens surface brightness in HST images
recipe.method: Residual sky subtraction using source masks and biweight location; PSF construction from stacked smoothed point sources; 2D parametric surface brightness decomposition (Sersic, de Vaucouleurs, Gaussian, exponential disk, PSF) or non-parametric isophotal fitting for edge-on disks; error estimation via Monte Carlo mock galaxy simulations.
key_parameters: Sersic index range [0.3, 10]; effective radius range [0.5 FWHM_PSF, +inf)
assumptions: Planck18 cosmology: H0 = 67.7 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_0,m = 0.31, Omega_0,Lambda = 0.69

recipe.goal: Derive global lens photometric properties and K-corrections
recipe.method: Compute curve of growth from 10^4 MC realizations of component parameters to derive R50, mu50, m_F110W, and C31 = R75/R25; measure aperture photometry of lensed background sources at 1.1 um; compute K-corrections using Brown Atlas elliptical templates.
assumptions: Cosmological surface brightness dimming factor (1 + z)^4; 17 local elliptical galaxy SED templates from Brown Atlas

recipe.goal: Perform gravitational lens modelling and background source reconstruction
recipe.method: Fit singular isothermal ellipsoid (SIE) mass model (plus external shear for S_3, S_19, S_40) and reconstruct background source using a preliminary Sersic parametric fit followed by a Voronoi pixelization with constant regularization.
key_parameters: Voronoi pixelization shape prior [20, 45] pixels; regularization coefficient lambda prior [10^-6, 10^6]; SNR > 3 threshold on source plane for magnification and circularised radius

answer_key.quantity: Number of confirmed strongly lensed systems (Class A)

evidence.quote: We confirm 65 systems to be lensed. Of these, 30 are new discoveries.

In conclusion, after the visual inspection of the HST images, use of ancillary data, and surface brightness modelling, we are able to assign 65 objects to class A, 67 to class B, 120 to class C, and 29 to class D.

answer_key.quantity: Number of newly discovered lensed systems

evidence.quote: We confirm 65 systems to be lensed. Of these, 30 are new discoveries.

answer_key.quantity: Median concentration index <C31> of modelled lenses

evidence.quote: We measure a median ⟨𝐶31⟩ = 6.8 ± 0.4, which is slightly higher than the median value ⟨𝐶31⟩ = 5.2 ± 0.1 measured by Watkins et al. (2022)

answer_key.quantity: Background source circularised radii range (1st to 99th percentile)

evidence.quote: However, the background source circularised radii (between 0.34 kpc and 1.30 kpc) are ∼3 times smaller than the ones measured in the sub-mm/mm for a similarly selected and partially overlapping sample.

The physical sizes of the background sources, measured as the circularised radii of the circles equivalent to the regions of the source plane with SNR > 3, range between 0.34 kpc (1-st percentile) and 1.30 kpc (99-th percentile).
At the same time, we find magnifications ranging between 2.4 (1-st percentile) and 15.8 (99-th percentile), with a median of 5.5 for our sample.

answer_key.quantity: Foreground lens mass within Einstein radius range (1st to 99th percentile)

evidence.quote: The mass within the Einstein radii of the foreground lenses ranges between 9.9 × 1010 M⊙ (1-st percentile) and 6.4 × 1011 M⊙ (99-th percentile).

answer_key.quantity: Foreground lens mass-to-light ratio in F110W within Einstein radius range

evidence.quote: The mass-to-light ratios in the F110W filter within the Einstein radius range between 1.25 and 8.86 M⊙ L−1 ⊙ .
